reasons.A: Right period register and semicolon-joined clauses, but sentences are shorter and plainer than the passage's long, qualified periods, with a few clipped modern beats ('It is a pleasure, or it is nothing').
reasons.B: Modern diction ('get out of our own heads', 'wellbeing'), short declarative sentences and almost no semicolons; the stance is conversational rather than the passage's measured, hedged Edwardian manner.
reasons.C: Closest sentence movement: long periods built from semicolon-linked clauses, hedging ('I am inclined myself', 'I confess', 'so far as I can see') and period diction like the passage; a touch ornate at the close (cat simile, rhetorical question) but not caricature.
